items.title: LeBron James and his fit with the 76ers
items.summary: The Decision 4.0 wasn't a grandiose television spectacle that captivated millions of viewers. Nor was it an emotional return home or an emboldened attempt to etch an imprint into a historic franchise's tapestry. LeBron James' resolution, choosing the Philadelphia 76ers as his fourth and final destination entering his 24th season, was a move not rooted in flash or pizazz but one centered in logic. In contention. "I still want to sacrifice," the 41-year-old said on his X account on what had been an eerily quiet Friday morning. "I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship."The tail end of James' three-part message — which in itself is a clear indication of the very online times society is in — offered some insight into the reasoning behind his…

items.title: 292 players will make more than LeBron James this NBA season. Here's the full list
items.summary: LeBron James signed with the Philadelphia 76ers in free agency as he looks to chase another NBA title before calling it a career. The 22-time All-Star took a significant pay cut to do so.After making nearly $53 million with the Los Angeles Lakers last season, James accepted a two-year contract worth the veteran minimum. The decision allowed Philadelphia – which already has two of the NBA's eight highest-paid players for 2026-27 in Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown – to be able to afford the 41-year-old superstar.James' new deal with the 76ers will be worth just under $8 million over two years. He is set to make just under $3.9 million in the first year of his contract, which will mark the least he has earned during a single NBA season, coming in just short of the $4.02 million he made during his rookie season in 2003-04.Just how cheap is James' deal for his first season in…

items.title: LeBron James' deal with the 76ers is a high school reunion with president of basketball operations Mike Gansey
items.summary: LeBron James' decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76erswill come with plenty of ripple effects. One of them is a full-circle moment involving the man he just handed a major win.The 41-year-old James will be reuniting with Mike Gansey, the 43-year-old president of basketball operations in Philadelphia. More than two decades ago, the two were competing for high school basketball honors in Ohio.Gansey was, in fact, the 2001 runner-up for Ohio's Mr. Basketball honors behind James when the future superstar won it as a sophomore, his first of three wins.Full circle moment for 76ers GM Mike Gansey and LeBron 🤯(📸 @SGAN30) pic.twitter.com/gt1Cg4H4n8— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) July 24, 2026The two never played each other, though, as far as we know. items.summary: Philadelphia was always on the list of teams LeBron James was seriously considering, but talking to executives and others at NBA Summer League and after, the 76ers were usually dismissed. They were fourth or fifth on people's lists. Great basketball fit, but was LeBron really going to end his career 2,700 miles away from his family, playing for a team he had never played for before?Yes, he is.LeBron James is joining the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year deal (at the veteran minimum, with a player option on the second year). Who were the winners and losers from this decision?
